sections.html:
Florence County lies in the Pee Dee region of northeastern South Carolina. The city of Florence is both the county seat and the largest community, and Johnsonville and Lake City are the other two municipalities. The county covers 804.28 square miles, 800.51 of them land, and the 2020 count was 137,059 people living in 54,627 households. Health care leads employment at 22.9 percent, followed by retail at 13.3 percent.

Where a house sits inside the county changes the bill. A property inside the city of Florence also carries city tax, with the rate set by City Council by June 30 each year, so two similar homes in different areas can owe different amounts. Read the millage lines on the bill, not just the county total.

Real estate and most personal property taxes are due by January 15. A deadline that falls on a weekend or holiday generally moves to the next business day. Bills usually go out around October.

The Auditor calculates taxes and applies penalties. The Treasurer must collect the full amount on the notice, so partial payments are refused. Postmarks are honored, and an outage of the online service does not delay a penalty. Receipts carry the date the payment is processed.

If title passed during the tax year, the notice went to the prior owner and the new owner got no timely notice, state law directs the treasurer to waive the penalties. Do not rely on that. After any sale, confirm the bill's mailing address with the Assessor.

sections.h2: How to pay and who to call
sections.html:
You can pay in person, by mail or online. Mail goes to Florence County Treasurer, P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501, and the county complex is at 180 N Irby Street, Florence, SC 29501. County offices there are open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

  • Treasurer: 843-665-3041. Collects the bill and also serves as tax collector.
  • Tax Assessor: 843-665-3056. Legal residence, address changes, mobile home registrations, deeds and plats.
  • Auditor: 843-665-3088. Homestead exemption, bill calculation and penalties.
  • Delinquent Tax Collection: 843-665-3095. Payoff amounts and tax sale redemption.

Cards are accepted in person with ID and a signature, with a processor fee of 1.7 percent plus $1. Online payments go through PayStar, which adds its own fee, and the official receipt arrives by mail in 5 to 10 business days. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid online. Use cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a card in person. The county's Treasurer page has the current details.

South Carolina requires every county to reassess all real property every five years at current market value. In a reassessment year a parcel's taxable value cannot rise more than 15 percent over five years unless an assessable transfer of interest occurs, which a sale usually causes.

When total values climb, the county must lower its millage to a rollback rate, though an individual bill can still go up or down. Owners are notified of changes of $1,000 or more.

Appeals go to the Tax Assessor in writing, and a PDF form is available on the county site. Ask the office which reassessment cycle covers your parcel before you plan around any deadline. Outside a notice window, state law lets you object in writing within 90 days after the assessor mails a notice. The county also offers qPublic for parcel records and a tax estimator, which help a buyer or seller see what a new owner might owe.

For a legal residence application, the Assessor's Office asks the applicant and spouse for a South Carolina driver's license or state ID, vehicle registration, a voter registration card where they apply, and a Social Security card. These requirements took effect June 20, 2016.

The Auditor's Office separately runs the Homestead Exemption Program and has an application form. Ask the Assessor how a new owner applies after a sale, and ask what date the application must be in by for the next bill.

Unpaid real property goes to a public auction run by the Delinquent Tax Office. The most recent sale began Monday, October 5, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., with a $10 bidder fee and pre-registration the business day before.

The owner or a mortgage holder has one year and a day to redeem. Owners of parcels sold in that sale have until October 6, 2027. Interest is added quarterly at 3, 6, 9 and 12 percent of the bid. If nobody redeems, a tax deed is issued. The county warns that it is not a warranty deed and that liens can remain.

Costs rise during the year. Recent amounts include $20 for delinquent notices in March, $30 for certified mail of a levy in April, $25 for advertising in August and $60 for a land mortgage search in October. Call 843-665-3095 to confirm the amount before paying, because dates and costs change.

sections.h2: Selling a Florence County house with tax owed
sections.html:
A sale and a tax balance can coexist. The title company can pay the balance from proceeds, as long as the payoff is current.

  1. Phone Delinquent Tax Collection at 843-665-3095 for the payoff.
  2. Ask the Assessor to confirm the mailing address and legal residence status.
  3. Check parcel records on qPublic and the flood status of the lot before you list.
  4. Keep Florence Regional Airport and the I-20 and I-95 junction in mind if you manage the sale from a distance, since both make the city easy to reach.

faqs.q: What is the Florence County property tax penalty schedule?
faqs.a: Tax unpaid after January 15 picks up 3 percent on January 16, another 7 percent on February 2 and another 5 percent on March 17, for 15 percent plus collection costs.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial property tax payment in Florence County?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer must collect the full amount on the tax notice, including penalties, and partial payments are refused.

faqs.q: Where is the Florence County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: The county complex is at 180 N Irby Street in Florence, and the Treasurer's phone is 843-665-3041. Mail payments to P.O. Box 100501, Florence, SC 29502-0501.

faqs.q: How long do I have to redeem a Florence County tax sale property?
faqs.a: The owner or mortgage holder has one year and a day after the sale. Interest is added in quarterly steps.

faqs.q: Who handles appeals in Florence County?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor takes appeals, which must be written. State law sets a 90 day window after the assessor mails a notice. Call 843-665-3056 for the current form.
